content: दुष् €4 <ab>P.</ab> (दुष्यति, दुष्ट) .²1 To be bad or corrupted, be spoiled or suffer damage. .²2 To be defiled or violated (as a woman <ab>&c.</ab>), be stained, be or become impure or contaminated; स्वल्पेनाप्यपकारेण ब्राह्मण्यमिव दुष्यति <ls>Pt. 1. 66</ls>; <ls>Ms. 7. 24</ls>, <ls n="Ms.">9. 318</ls>, <ls n="Ms.">10. 102</ls>. .²3 To sin, commit a mistake, be wrong. .²4 To be unchaste or faithless. --{%<ab>Caus.</ab>%} (दूषयति-ते, but दूषयति-ते or दोषयति-ते in the sense of ‘making depraved’ or ‘corrupting’) .²1 To corrupt, spoil, cause to perish, hurt, destroy, defile, taint, contaminate, vitiate, pollute (<ab>lit.</ab> and <ab>fig.</ab>); न भीतो मरणादस्मि केवलं दूषितं यशः <ls>Mk. 10. 27</ls>; पूरा दूषयति स्थलीम् <ls>R. 12. 30</ls>, <ls n="R.">8. 68</ls>, <ls n="R.">10. 47</ls>, <ls n="R.">12. 4</ls>; <ls>Ms. 5. 1</ls>, <ls n="Ms. 5.">104</ls>, <ls n="Ms.">7. 195</ls>; <ls>Y. 1. 189</ls>; <ls>Amaru. 72</ls>; न त्वेवं दूषयिष्यामि शस्त्रग्रहमहाव्रतम् <ls>Mv. 3. 8</ls> ‘shall not sully, violate or break <ab>&c.</ab>’ .²2 To corrupt the morals, demoralize. .²3 To violate or dishonour (as a girl or anotherʼs wife); योऽकामां दूषयेत्कन्यां स सद्यो वधमर्हति <ls>Ms. 8. 364</ls>, <ls n="Ms. 8.">368</ls>. .²4 To abrogate, rescind, annul. .²5 To blame, censure, find fault with, speak ill of, accuse; दूषितः सर्वलोकेषु निषादत्वं गमिष्यति <ls>Rām.</ls>; <ls>Y. 1. 66</ls>. .²6 To adulterate. .²7 To falsify. .²8 To refute, disprove.
